articles.title: ‘What is this emotion telling me?’ How anger, fear and jealousy can point the way to a better life
articles.summary: It’s tempting to ignore uncomfortable feelings – but maybe they’re the key to a happier, more successful future. Time to increase your psychological flexibility … Something infuriating happened to me recently.
body: Obviously, I could have brainstormed alternatives, from going for a run outside or taking an online class to – simple plan – joining one of the five other gyms in my neighbourhood. But instead I chose to see the inconvenience of it all. I grew creakier and crankier by the day.

Eventually, I forced myself to find a new venue. It’s cleaner, friendlier and a third of the price. It’s also further away, but I reframed my grumpiness about that by incorporating the extra walk into my warmup.

I didn’t realise it at the time but what I was grappling with is a concept known as psychological flexibility. And it is being cited as a powerful strategy that can help us to persevere with our goals. So what does it actually involve?

Unlike positive thinking, then, psychological flexibility is about acknowledging rather than drowning out or denying uncomfortable feelings such as anger, anxiety or fear, and using them as feedback for action. It’s also about letting yourself off the hook when you face insurmountable obstacles, unlike another pop psychology model, grit, which is characterised by powering through, no matter what.
points: It’s tempting to ignore uncomfortable feelings – but maybe they’re the key to a happier, more successful future.

articles.title: From the overblown to the ordinary? Met Gala 2027 to celebrate ‘poetics of everyday’
articles.summary: Event regarded as Oscars of fashion industry replaces John Galliano retrospective with homage to the ‘extra ordinary’ A few months after the planned John Galliano Met Gala retrospective was cancelled amid a backlash focused on the designer’s past, a more commonplace theme has been announced: “…
body: While the dress code for the next Met Gala, which will be held on 3 May 2027, is yet to be announced, it traditionally derives from the exhibition theme.

According to a press release, extraORDINARY will “explore how designers rework familiar garments, everyday objects, and commonplace materials”. Taking wardrobe staples and everyday materials – “from jeans, T-shirts and puffer coats to paper, plastic and metal” – it will “examine how design reveals unexpected possibilities within everyday things”.

Reactions have been mixed. For Dana Thomas, the author of Gods and Kings: The Rise and Fall of Alexander McQueen and John Galliano, it “reinforces the message that was very, very clear with the Galliano announcement that the costume institute’s team is highly out of touch”. She characterises the decision to “take such ordinary garments and then show how fashion has co-opted them and added zeros to the price tag” as tone deaf.

articles.title: This Is What Winter 2026 Has in Store for Every Star Sign, According to an Astrologer
articles.summary: With plenty of retrogrades, eclipses, and planetary shake-ups, this winter could bring drama and breakthroughs. Read your winter 2026 horoscopes here.
body: It’s been a chaotic time, but the end of autumn finds Mercury and Venus ushering in a fresh start under the twinkling holiday lights following their retrogrades. To explain: each retrograde has a “post-shadow,” which essentially means a bit of a paradigm shift. Mercury rules communication, while Venus rules love and money, so conversations around these themes might finally feel less muddled and more smooth-sailing. Enmeshments may untangle, responsibilities may firm up, and reciprocity may finally be restored.

As ever, the winter solstice arrives on December 21, marking the shortest day of the year and the start of Capricorn season, a sign that urges us to think practically and long-term. This isn’t just about dreaming up New Year’s resolutions: the Sun in Capricorn asks us big questions about how we want to invest our time and energy, and what we want to build for our future, so there’ll be a lot of that this winter.
points: With plenty of retrogrades, eclipses, and planetary shake-ups, this winter could bring drama and breakthroughs.

articles.title: ‘AI clog’: UK public bodies battle onslaught of chatbot-generated complaints
articles.summary: MPs, local authorities, lawyers, schools and more are receiving floods of grievances, requests and legal challenges, often complex to read and respond to. “It started as a trickle in 2024 and now it’s an onslaught.” Hollie Wickens, a senior caseworker in a Labour MP’s office, is explaining the…
body: “Half the emails we receive are some form of AI,” she says, adding that this has made requests and complaints much more complex and time-consuming to read and deal with, despite her decade of experience in the role. “It is definitely more taxing.”

At the start of this decade, applying for a job, writing a complaint or objecting to a local planning application typically required considerable effort: time to research a topic, fill in a form or write a formal-sounding email, with specialist knowledge often also required.

That was until the rapid growth of ChatGPT – which turns four later this month – Claude, Copilot, Gemini and other generative AI tools over the past couple of years. These chatbots are helping turn laypeople into experts by giving access to a free – albeit sometimes unreliable – legal adviser, administrator or personal assistant.

articles.title: Walking with spirits in Cambodia’s sacred forests
articles.summary: Former loggers and poachers have embraced ancient traditions to promote and protect the Cardamom Mountains’ ever-threatened natural wonders. I’m two hours downriver from the Chi Phat community ecotourism camp, in the Koh Kong region of Cambodia, when my phone signal fizzles out completely.
body: As well as its plant and protection initiatives, it is also known for its storied history, from ancient burial grounds to the last stronghold of Pol Pot’s fleeing Khmer Rouge fighters into the late 1980s. If trees could talk … Well, many believe these ones can.

Unlike the western way of managing belief – sealed in gated graveyards or glimpsed on infrequent Sundays – Khmer spirituality (as with the national, Buddhist faith) is as integral to daily Cambodian life as the ticking-over tuk-tuk or the churn of the streetside sugarcane crusher. The Cardamoms has long been a land I have tried to reach. I’m here for a few days, hoping to feel the spiritual power of such a sacred place, as well as check out its diverse yet elusive wildlife, from forest elephants to wild dogs (or dholes ).

In Cambodian animism, neak ta are powerful, just spirits who protect and watch over the country’s boundless, ever-threatened natural wonders: from the mighty Tonlé Sap River, one of the few in the world that reverses its flow twice yearly but is threatened by increasing pollution, to its dense, diverse, frequently devastated forests.

articles.title: Beauty Marks: The Best Beauty Looks of the Week
articles.summary: From Sienna Miller’s romantic blurred lip to Kate Young’s diamond-studded chignon, this week’s best beauty looks were all in the details.
body: Welcome back to Beauty Marks: Vogue ’s weekly edition of the best moments in celebrity beauty, from Vogue editors’ IG feeds, and all the glam of the fashion and pop culture landscapes. Each week, we curate the nail art to pin for your next nail appointment, new recruits to ‘Team Bob’, and major red carpet moments from the week’s most glamorous affairs. As always, it’s as much about celebrity beauty as it is about the makeup artists, hairstylists, and nail artists, as well as the creators crafting the trends you’re about to see everywhere.

This week in beauty was a study in contrasts: sculptural hair met soft-focus makeup, while barely-there lips shared the spotlight with high-impact eyes. Sienna Miller made a romantic case for the blurred lip, Emily Blunt embraced a wintry shade of blonde, and Kim Petras dialed up the drama with graphic liner and ice-blonde bangs. Elsewhere, Kate Young turned a diamond into the ultimate hair accessory, Kris Jenner revisited the razor-sharp bob, and Lily Allen served up a masterclass in hair transformations. From elaborate nail art to gravity-defying chignons, there was plenty to look twice at.
points: From Sienna Miller’s romantic blurred lip to Kate Young’s diamond-studded chignon, this week’s best beauty looks were all in the details.

articles.title: A Costa Rican Beach Resort with a World-Class Coffee Program
articles.summary: The roastery at Nekajui on the Papagayo Peninsula shows off the country’s rich coffee culture.
body: In Hotels With Great Taste, we’re pulling back the curtain for a peek at the “special sauce” that hotels use to create memorable, meaningful culinary experiences for their guests.

Check-in at Nekajui on Costa Rica’s verdant Papagayo Peninsula happens inside a sparsely furnished bungalow the staff call La Casita. But walk across the drive, past a massive ceiba tree hung heavy with lanterns, and all humility vanishes. The whole property sweeps out before you: an endless green lawn, pools cascading down two levels, and, finally, the serenely sparkling bay beyond.

Nekajui is Ritz Carlton’s first Reserve resort in Central or South America. The Reserve’s are Ritz Carlton’s nod to the idea of complete escape, often in the far flung retreats—the Chinese Himalayas, or the Saudi Arabian desert.

Now, the recently opened Nekajui allows you to unwind on the lush Costa Rican coast teeming with wildlife like capuchins, coatis, and iguanas. Hidden away at the remote property, you’ll also find a local coffee program that’s on par with the best big city cafes in the world.
points: The roastery at Nekajui on the Papagayo Peninsula shows off the country’s rich coffee culture.

articles.title: 20 Food Advent Calendars to Buy Before They Sell Out (2026)
articles.summary: From cookies and chocolates to wine and cheese, these are the best food advent calendars to buy in 2026.
body: Nothing sparks joy and jumpstarts the Christmas season like a food advent calendar. You get 25 tiny compartments, each housing a festive treat hidden behind a perforated door. They’re not just chocolate anymore. These days, they’re filled with everything from gummies and chili crisp to whiskey and coffee. And if you’re thinking of ordering one to enjoy this year, the time is now. December 1st is only seven weeks away, and after reporting on these things for the past five years, we’ve seen these calendars sell out months in advance or get backordered every year.

The best advent calendars contain high-quality sweets, booze, condiments, snacks, teas, or coffees you’ll be genuinely excited to open every day. And who knows, they might even introduce you to a product you’ll want to buy on repeat once the holiday season has come and gone.
